setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I already heard a couple of things from Kim'; prospect: 'like I told Cam, I have a newborn at home'

prospect.name: Sean Feeney
prospect.training_background: Working out since high school, self-described 'consistently inconsistent'; does some kettlebell swings; never had a trainer
prospect.medical: Bilateral hip pain, right hip onset ~1 year ago described as 'feels like sciatica', left hip now same; left shoulder 'went out' a few months ago and remains painful, right shoulder now compensating and beginning to fail. Physical therapy appointment not until mid-August 2026 — not yet assessed by any clinician.

signals: 23 but 'I move like I'm 40 right now'
Wants his former function back: 'get that back to actually feeling 23'
Carries regret about taking prior fitness for granted: 'I kind of took it for granted'

goals.text: Get his mobility back — stop moving like a 40-year-old at 23
Build functional strength for work and life
Better conditioning so the firefighting job is less exhausting and more enjoyable
Be consistent on his own accord outside of work
Be able to care for and be a role model for his newborn son Milo

pains.text: Bilateral hip pain (sciatica-like) and a left shoulder that went out, right shoulder now compensating; takes 30-40 seconds to get up off the ground
Pain is starting to threaten his ability to do his job
Struggles to hold his newborn son because of the shoulder
Cannot start the workout — getting in the car and going to the gym is where he falls through
Never had anyone holding him accountable, dissatisfied with own results
Eats out once or twice a week, aware nutrition has room for improvement

objections.raw_quote: Shoof. Damn. Huh. That is steep. That's a lot steeper than I was thinking.
objections.rep_response: Isolated the objection ('do you feel like if you had the money, you would do it?'), asked what was left over monthly and whether anything was set aside, then pivoted to an unlisted lower-priced self-serve programme

objections.raw_quote: If I had the money you have, but I don't, I just, I don't, I don't make that much.
objections.rep_response: Asked for monthly surplus ($400-500) and existing savings, then offered a $1,000/6mo or $200/mo self-serve programme

objections.raw_quote: I wouldn't be able to figure it out today, basically. It's where I'm at with it.
objections.rep_response: Pushed for a decision deadline, agreed to two weeks with a check-in call next week, assigned budget review as homework

offer.payment_plan_terms: For the unlisted self-serve programme only: $1,000 upfront for six months, or $200/month for six months totalling $1,200. Rep stated the $1,000 would later be credited toward the full Trevor coaching. No payment plan was offered against the $6,000 coaching itself.

evidence: Prospect: 'I'd have to kind of look at my budget... I wouldn't be able to figure it out today'
Agreed a decision window: 'Could I get, like, two weeks?' with rep calling next week
Counter-evidence: prospect said of the cheaper tier 'Yeah, that's a lot better' and 'I could see myself doing that' — genuine interest, but no commitment and no payment link sent
Prospect's stated ceiling was $150/month, below even the $200/month instalment offered
outcome.next_step: Prospect reviews his budget; rep calls in one week, decision by two weeks

notable.note: Prospect disclosed active, worsening bilateral hip and shoulder injuries with a physical therapy appointment still six weeks out, and the rep responded by asserting the programme would work — 'it's not like with your hips, your shoulders, you wouldn't be able to do it' — without asking whether any clinician had cleared him. A price outside the two published tiers was constructed live ($1,000/6mo, $200/mo).

quality.notes: Frequent turn-level swaps throughout; several rep questions are attributed to Sean Feeney and vice versa (e.g. the 'why him?' question at 00:11:15 and the price-reaction block around 00:30:56-00:32:20 are inverted). Roles resolved from content. The word 'Fathom' appears several times as an ASR artefact substituted for other words.
